title: Everyman
author: Hugo von Hofmannsthal
description: Jedermann: Hofmannsthal’s version of an old English morality play, in which Death comes for a rich man and his friends desert him. It has been performed outdoors in front of the cathedral at the festival since 1920.

title: The World of Yesterday
author: Stefan Zweig
description: Stefan Zweig’s memoir of the lost world of Austria before 1914, written in exile. He describes his years in Salzburg, where famous friends came to visit, and how he could see Hitler’s home across the border from his house on the hill.

title: The Story of the Trapp Family Singers
author: Maria Augusta Trapp
description: Maria von Trapp’s own account of leaving Nonnberg Abbey to look after a widowed naval captain’s children, marrying him, and taking the family singing around the world after they left Austria. It is less sweet than the film.

title: Mozart: The Reign of Love
author: Jan Swafford
description: Composer and writer Jan Swafford’s long biography, which spends its early chapters in Salzburg: Mozart’s father Leopold, the tours, and Mozart’s growing hatred of the town and its archbishop.

title: Gathering Evidence
author: Thomas Bernhard
description: Five short memoirs by the Austrian writer Thomas Bernhard, translated by David McLintock. He went to school in Salzburg during the war, and his portrait of the city, its Catholic schools, and its Nazi past is famously bitter.

title: Across
author: Peter Handke
description: Der Chinese des Schmerzes: Peter Handke’s short novel about a teacher in Salzburg who commits a sudden act of violence. Handke, later a Nobel laureate, lived on the Mönchsberg in the 1980s.
